title: fix(pm): make dispatch-gates honest about its residue, and match watch hints on segment boundaries
body:
Fixes #8632
Fixes #8534

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` ended with a hand-written list of three gate names and called it "the rest". This makes the residue derived instead, and carries the declared rider from the on-hold `hintCovers` card, which the same file surface triggered.

## What the measurement changed about the card

The card frames the residue as "three judgement-call gates, already out of sync by at least one (`check:where-matcher`)". Re-measured at `5e78db282`, that framing is too small, and the correction decided the mechanism.

All four gates under discussion land in a bucket the output has never mentioned. `classifyEntry` produces three verdicts; the run printed `matched` and a count of `undetermined`, and said nothing at all about `silent`:

```
family                        verdict   its entire hint set
check:where-matcher           silent    scripts/where-matcher-conformance.baseline.json, origin/main
check:engine-double-contract  silent    scripts/engine-double-contract.baseline.json, @objectstack/{core,objectql,metadata-core}
check:query-options-erasure   silent    scripts/query-options-erasure-baseline.json, origin/main
check:nul-bytes               silent    .claude/agents/os-dev.md, scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs
```

Not one of those literals can cover a card's path. The families have hints, so the "undetermined" bucket never sees them; the hints cover nothing, so the matched column never sees them either. That is the one output shape the file's own header forbids ("a gate the derivation cannot mention at all"), and on a two-path card it applied to 55 of 98 families, not to three.

Two consequences:

- **the residue is 90 families, not 3.** A prose enumeration kept in sync with that is not a thing anyone can maintain, so option 2 as the card states it — a guard holding the closing prose against the `check:*` population — is not available. The honest move is to stop enumerating.
- **the deleted sentence was a second copy.** `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` carries the same list at L144-145 and names four gates where this named three (it also has `.claude/agents/**` gives `check:agent-model-declared`). The two copies had already drifted. A second copy of a list rotting inside prose is the incident this file's header cites as its reason for embedding no list of checks — reproduced in the file's last sentence.

## What landed

**1. The three test-file ratchets now derive together.** `check:engine-double-contract` and `check:where-matcher` join `check:query-options-erasure` in `CHANGE_KIND_GATES`. The deciding evidence is not the three logged incidents but a structural identity with an entry already in the table: all three walk the tree for `*.test.*` files (`check-engine-double-contract.mjs` line 342, `check-where-matcher-conformance.mjs` line 562) and reconcile against a shrink-only baseline, and all three name only that baseline. Naming one of three and calling the other two a judgement call was an inconsistency in the table, not a considered line.

The noise objection recorded on the card is answered by what the gates cost rather than by narrowing the trigger: each is a whole-tree shrink-only ratchet, so one run answers for the entire repo, needs no build, and prints the offending file and line. The trigger deliberately does not read file contents to confirm a double is present — a card is dispatched before its code exists, so the double the gate will object to is usually not on disk yet.

End to end on the path from the logged instances:

```
$ node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.keys.test.ts
  adds or edits a test file: packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.keys.test.ts
    - pnpm check:query-options-erasure   ...
    - pnpm check:type-check-coverage     ...
    - pnpm check:type-check-debt         ...
    - pnpm check:engine-double-contract  ...   <- new
    - pnpm check:where-matcher           ...   <- new
```

**2. The closing prose is replaced by `residueLines()`** — derived counts for every bucket, no gate named, and it throws when the three verdicts do not account for every discovered family. A fourth bucket added to `classifyEntry` and not wired in would otherwise shrink the residue silently, which is this card's failure class.

**3. `silent` is printed for the first time,** with the note that it is the derivation's weakest claim. `--residue` lists the unplaced families runnably, each with the hints its exclusion rests on — so `check:where-matcher` now reads as `names: scripts/where-matcher-conformance.baseline.json, origin/main`, and the weakness is visible rather than inferred.

**4. Census guard.** Every name in `CHANGE_KIND_GATES` is asserted against the live workflow population by the self-test, not only by the run that prints STALE. That table is the one enumerable list in the file, so it is the one a guard can hold. Reverse-verified: renaming an entry to `check:where-matcher-v2` fails the case with `(missing: check:where-matcher-v2)` while the live run still prints STALE — the two mechanisms compose.

No `lint.yml` wiring was needed: `check:pm-dispatch-gates` already runs this file's `--self-test`, so extending the self-test is the CI wiring.

## Rider (#8534): segment boundaries, and the trade decided

`hintCovers` compared raw string prefixes, so a hint claimed any sibling sharing its name prefix. The card filed this as dormant on a census of 324 hints against 73 package directories. Re-measured here against all 5940 tracked files rather than package directories only, **it is not dormant** — one answer changes across 354 live hints:

```
hint 'content/docs' vs 'content/docs.site.json'   raw=true  segment=false
    <- check:role-word, check:docs-audit-scope
```

`content/docs.site.json` is a real file beside the `content/docs` directory, and neither gate reads it. The class was live all along; the earlier census probed directories and this specimen is a file.

### The collapsed-glob reach trade — decided, not assumed

Globs collapse by deletion, so `packages/client*` becomes `packages/client`. As a glob it would legitimately match a sibling `packages/client-react`; under the segment rule it no longer reaches it. **Decision: refuse the reach.** Grounds:

- **measured need.** Exactly two live hints carry a partial-segment glob, and both are npm package specifiers rather than repo paths: `@objectstack/spec@*` (check:release-page-status) and `@fx/spec*` (check:type-source-resolution). No repo path begins with `@`, so both are inert either way. The capability this trade would protect has zero live instances — a `packages/client*` hint is hypothetical, not something the tree has.
- **one rule, not two.** Preserving glob reach means re-deriving, at comparison time, information the collapse deliberately destroys — a second matching mode keyed on syntax that is already gone by the time the function runs.
- **error directions are not symmetric.** Refusing costs a missing lead (one card, one CI round); preserving costs a fabricated lead, pasted into every prompt whose surface brushes it. Refusal errs in the direction the file's header calls safe.

Pinned in both directions, so the decision reads as an assertion rather than as this paragraph: the collapsed glob does not reach the sibling, and it still covers the package it names. If a real `packages/client*`-shaped hint ever appears and the reach is wanted, the answer is to spell the hint as the two paths it means, not to widen the comparison back to a string prefix.

### The coupled second half

The rider's trailing-dot half is not cosmetic — it is required by the boundary rule. One live hint carries a sentence period (`check-skill-compatibility-version.mjs` line 295 spells its own filename as the last word of a sentence, in a module-body array element that comment masking cannot reach). It reached its real file only through the raw-prefix branch the boundary rule removes:

```
raw prefix (before)         -> true
segment rule, not stripped  -> false      <- the coupling
segment rule, stripped      -> true
```

So extraction now trims a trailing run of dots and slashes, at the point the hint is built. Both halves of #8534 are done, which is why this closes it.

## Verification — all at `5e78db282`, the final commit

```
node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test    136 cases pass  (107 on origin/main, +29)
pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates                      pass  (the derived gate for this file surface)
node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs --self-test      75 assertions pass
node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs                  OK, 5935 text files, no control bytes
npx eslint scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs          exit 0
pnpm check:pm-skill-id-lint                       pass
pnpm check:pm-half-states                         pass
pnpm check:ratchet-remedy-authority               pass
pnpm check:partof-closing-keyword                 pass
```

Gate union re-derived from the actual changed paths with the post-change script (which exercises this fix): `check:pm-dispatch-gates` is the only path-matched family, and no convention kind hits (the changed file is not a test file). The type-check ratchets cannot move: no tsconfig in the tree sets `allowJs`, so a `.mjs` file is outside every tsc program.

Reverse verification, each direction predicted before running and restored after:

| ablation | predicted | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| trailing-dot trim removed | 5 red, including the live coupling pin | 5 red, exactly those |
| segment rule reverted to raw prefix | 4 red (siblings + the trade), the boundary-glob cases stay green | 4 red, exactly those |
| a table entry renamed | census guard red, naming the missing gate; live run still STALE | both, as predicted |

## Not in scope

The detector's `Object.assign` blind spot recorded on #8553 is inherited, not addressed here. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` and `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` are untouched — the SKILL.md guard-index line already describes this script generically, and no fix here needed text in either.
